relevance_reason: The paper reports heterozygous TNNI3 missense mutations in autosomal dominant familial DCM. That is the same gene as CMD2A but a different, dominant phenotype, so it is useful mainly as context or heterogeneity for the autosomal recessive entry.

findings.statement: Carballo et al. (2009) screened 96 probands with dilated cardiomyopathy for TNNI3 mutations and reported the first autosomal dominant DCM-causing mutations in TNNI3. This adds TNNI3 to the genes in which different mutations can cause either hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy.
quotes: To test TNNI3 as a candidate gene, a panel of 96 probands with DCM was analyzed.

These are the first reported autosomal dominant DCM-causing mutations in TNNI3, and so the findings expand the spectrum of disease-causing genes that lead to either hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or DCM depending on the specific mutation.

findings.statement: Carballo et al. (2009) described 5 carriers of TNNI3 mutations from families with severe, early-onset familial dilated cardiomyopathy. Three of the 5 needed cardiac transplantation, at ages 6, 15, and 24 years.
quotes: each associated with severe and early onset familial DCM
Of the 5 mutation carriers, cardiac transplantation was required in 3, at ages 6, 15, and 24 years.

findings.statement: Carballo et al. (2009) used heteroduplex analysis and sequencing to identify a novel TNNI3 missense mutation, lys36-to-gln (K36Q), in a family with severe, early-onset dilated cardiomyopathy. The variant was evaluated by segregation analysis and in normal controls. Troponin reconstituted with the mutant troponin I gave a lower maximum ATPase rate and lower Ca(2+) sensitivity than wildtype, and mutant thin filaments had reduced Ca(2+) affinity.
quotes: We report 2 novel TNNI3 missense mutations, Lys36Gln and Asn185Lys, each associated with severe and early onset familial DCM.
Exons with aberrant profiles were sequenced and variants evaluated by segregation analysis and study of normal controls.
troponin reconstituted with either mutant troponin I gave lower maximum ATPase rates and lower Ca(2+) sensitivity than wild type

findings.statement: Carballo et al. (2009) identified a second novel TNNI3 missense mutation, asn185-to-lys (N185K), in a family with severe, early-onset familial dilated cardiomyopathy. In functional studies, troponin containing the mutant troponin I gave a lower maximum actin-tropomyosin-activated myosin ATPase rate and lower Ca(2+) sensitivity than wildtype, and mutant thin filaments had reduced Ca(2+) affinity.
quotes: We report 2 novel TNNI3 missense mutations, Lys36Gln and Asn185Lys, each associated with severe and early onset familial DCM.
Furthermore, mutant thin filaments had reduced Ca(2+) affinity compared with normal.

findings.statement: Carballo et al. (2009) noted that the functional changes caused by the TNNI3 mutations, lower ATPase rates and reduced Ca(2+) sensitivity, closely matched a consistent phenotype seen with proven DCM mutations in other thin filament proteins. They took this as support that the mutations are disease-causing.
quotes: The functional alterations mirror closely a consistent phenotype found in proven DCM mutations in other thin filament proteins, thus supporting the interpretation that these mutations are disease-causing.

relevance_reason: Reports a novel TNNI3 mutation causing autosomal recessive idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy in a family, defining CMD2A.

findings.statement: Murphy et al. (2004) screened the cardiac troponin I gene (TNNI3) in 235 patients with dilated cardiomyopathy, using mutation analysis suitable for identifying both dominant and recessive mutations, and identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease. The authors stated that TNNI3 was the first recessive gene identified for this condition.
quotes: We used mutation analysis suitable for identification of both dominant and recessive mutations to investigate the sarcomeric gene for cardiac troponin I (TNNI3) in 235 patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.
We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
TNNI3 is the first recessive gene identified for this condition

findings.statement: Murphy et al. (2004) found in functional studies that the recessive TNNI3 mutation impaired troponin interactions, which they suggested could lead to diminished myocardial contractility.
quotes: Functional studies showed impairment of troponin interactions that could lead to diminished myocardial contractility.

findings.statement: Murphy et al. (2004) suggested that other recessive genes for idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy could be identified by mutation analyses designed to detect homozygous mutations.
quotes: we suggest that other such genes could be pinpointed by mutation analyses designed to identify homozygous mutations.

relevance_reason: Clinical series and complex segregation analysis showing autosomal recessive inheritance of infantile dilated cardiomyopathy in Saudi Arab families.

findings.statement: Seliem et al. (2000) evaluated 55 consecutive cases of dilated cardiomyopathy diagnosed by echocardiography in patients younger than 10 years of age, seen over a 5-year period in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. They came from 41 families of Arab descent and made up 20% of the offspring of those families. In 95% of cases, age at presentation was under 30 months (range, 1 to 100 months); 38% were male and 62% female.
quotes: We evaluated 55 consecutive cases of dilated cardiomyopathy in patients <10 y of age seen during a 5-y interval. Echocardiography was the primary diagnostic modality.
The 55 cases represented 20% of the offspring of 41 families of Arab descent.
Age at presentation was <30 mo (95%) (range, 1 to 100 mo); males (38%) and females (62%) were affected.
findings.population: Arab; Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia

findings.statement: In the series of Seliem et al. (2000), 25 patients (46%) died, 15 (27%) improved, and 15 (27%) recovered. At diagnosis, the left ventricular shortening fraction ranged from 5 to 28% and did not differ among the patients who died, improved, or recovered.
quotes: Patients died (25 patients, 46%), improved (15 patients, 27%), or recovered (15 patients, 27%).
The left ventricular shortening fraction at diagnosis ranged from 5 to 28% and did not differ in those who died, improved, or recovered.
findings.population: Arab; Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia

findings.statement: Seliem et al. (2000) found that the parents were first cousins in 19 of the 41 families (46%), with no obvious consanguinity in the other 22 (54%). A complex segregation analysis of the family data using the mixed model of inheritance showed that recessive inheritance fit the data best. The authors suggested that recessive dilated cardiomyopathy may be hard to recognize in populations where consanguineous marriage is uncommon and families have few children.
quotes: In 19 families (46%), parents were first cousins; there was no obvious consanguinity in 22 families (54%).
Complex segregation analysis of the family data using the mixed model of inheritance showed that a model of recessive inheritance best fits the data.

Recessively inherited dilated cardiomyopathy has been infrequently reported, perhaps because it may be difficult to recognize in other patient groups in which consanguineous marriage is uncommon and the number of children per family is small.
findings.population: Arab; Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia

findings.statement: Goldblatt et al. (1987) described idiopathic, isolated dilated cardiomyopathy in 3 members of a consanguineous Madeira Portuguese family.
quotes: we describe a form of autosomal recessively inherited, dilated, cardiomyopathy occurring in three members of a consanguineous Madeira Portuguese family

findings.statement: Goldblatt et al. (1987) concluded that dilated cardiomyopathy in a consanguineous Madeira Portuguese family was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. They noted that familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy is usually reported as autosomal dominant with variable penetrance and expressivity. After reviewing the literature, they suggested that the autosomal recessive form is more common than previously reported.
quotes: Familial, isolated, dilated cardiomyopathy is usually reported as being inherited in an autosomal dominant mode with variable penetrance and expressivity.
Following review of the literature, it appears that the autosomal recessive form of dilated cardiomyopathy is more common than previously reported.

findings.statement: Goldblatt et al. (1987) noted that cardiomyopathy is a heterogeneous disorder with many inherited and acquired causes.
quotes: Cardiomyopathy is a heterogeneous disorder with numerous inherited and acquired causes.
